newsitem.title: PERU: Shots heard at Peru hostage crisis site - radio.
newsitem.headline: Shots heard at Peru hostage crisis site - radio.

text.p: A number of shots were heard at the site of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima early on Wednesday where heavily armed Marxist rebels hold 73 hostages, local radio said.
Local RPP radio station said several bursts of gunfire were heard coming from the diplomatic compound at about 1:00 a.m. EST (0600 GMT).
The shots were immediately followed by silence. Police surrounding the residence moved into a state of alert but did not approach the compound, witnesses said.
Reuters photographers stationed around the residence said they heard at least one burst of about five rounds from the rear of the residence.

Earlier in the day, police guarding the area had moved to within a few yards (meters) of the front of the property in a series of unexplained manoeuvres, while some police threw rocks into the driveway. The purpose of this was unclear.

The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels inside the diplomatic mansion have fired what were later described by police as warning shots on several occasions during the 36-day siege. The previous incidents caused alarm but no injuries, authorities said.
